baslik: Why Rockets Explode on the Launch Pad
aciklama:
A rocket is a controlled explosion pointed at the sky - and the line between launch and disaster is razor thin. Here is why they blow up.

#shorts #space #engineering #science #rockets

sahneler.metin: A rocket is a controlled explosion. Lose control, and it explodes.
A tiny crack can turn it into a fireball in one second.
So why is the balance so fragile?
Inside are hundreds of tons of fuel and oxidizer.
They must burn together in precise balance.
A stuck valve, and the fuel ignites all at once.
The thin metal tanks simply burst.
Every explosion teaches engineers how to fly the next one.

vaka.tetik: a tiny crack or a stuck valve
vaka.mekanizma: uncontrolled propellant ignition and tank overpressure
vaka.ders: every failure feeds the next design
vaka.yanilgi: Many launch failures aren't explosions at first — the vehicle breaks up, or range safety destroys it on purpose.
vaka.tartisma: Is it better to fly early and fail often, or test exhaustively on the ground first?
